opening_message:
Ticket 1: Diana Cooper (employee ID E020) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E020.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: admin
  - comment: Diana Cooper (E020) is a full-time Engineer. She requests admin access to Source Code. As a full-time employee whose role (Engineer) owns the Source Code system, admin is permitted, so I recommend granting admin.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Diana Cooper (E020) is a contractor with basic security training (discrepancy with HR note claiming full-time Engineer). Contractors can never have admin; with basic training the maximum is read. Requested admin exceeds the maximum, so I recommend granting read.
reason: The two notes conflict on Diana Cooper's (E020) employment type: HR claims full-time Engineer, while Security claims contractor with basic security training. Granting admin would require the full-time Engineer role-owns-system exception, but the Security note explicitly flags a discrepancy and states she is a contractor, and contractors can never be granted admin. Under the contractor policy with basic training, the maximum allowed is read, and the requested admin exceeds that maximum. Granting read is the safe, policy-compliant level given the unresolved conflict.
